STEP 1 - Scene: A snack of raw/roasted almonds (whole, brown-skinned nuts) on a plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white plate, roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 314 cm² (treating it as a round-equivalent; the square is about 20x20 = 400 cm², so I use ~350 cm² of usable surface).

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds only.

STEP 4 - Area: Almonds cover a pile in the upper-left/top portion of the plate, roughly 20% of the plate's visible surface.

STEP 5 - Volume: Covered area ≈ 70 cm² x typical pile height ~1.5 cm (nuts piled a few layers) ≈ 105 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole almonds are dense-ish but with gaps; bulk density ~0.55 g/ml (nuts are not a dense solid, but are not loose leaves either). 105 ml x 0.55 ≈ 58 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds ≈ 580 kcal per 100 g (raw/dry-roasted). 58 g x 5.8 ≈ 336 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 40 to 50 almonds visible, each roughly 1.2 g, which gives roughly 50 to 60 g. Consistent with 58 g and about 340 kcal.

Total: about 58 g, about 340 kcal.
